title: 1911 Portuguese presidential election
summary: On 24 August 1911, three days after promulgating the constitution, the Constituent Assembly sitting as the Congress of the Republic elected Manuel de Arriaga the first president of the Portuguese Republic, for a term of four years. The constitution had put the choice in parliament’s hands rather than the electorate’s and had left the office deliberately weak — no government of its own, no popular mandate — but it kept the power to appoint and dismiss ministers. Arriaga used that power in January 1915 to dismiss the Democratic government and call General Pimenta de Castro, who then ruled without the Chamber: the first time the Republic’s own constitution was turned against its parliamentary majority. He resigned in May 1915, twelve days after the rising that undid the experiment. It is in the atlas because the presidency it filled is where the First Republic’s crises were settled, and mostly by force.
